surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the adsorption of the Hf precursor onto the substrate, followed by a self-limiting reaction without gas-phase interactions. The reaction between the Hf precursor and the substrate reaches a self-limiting mode, resulting in a controlled growth rate. The Hf-O bond in Hf/H20849mp/H208504 was more stable than the Hf-N bond in Hf/H20849NEt2/H208504, and the bulky OCMeEt2 ligand in Hf/H20849mp/H208504 was more effective in shielding the Hf atoms than the NEt2 ligand in Hf/H20849NEt2/H208504.
evidence: The Hf/H20849mp/H208504 samples had a lower saturated growth rate and wider ALD process temperatures than the Hf/H20849NEt2/H208504 samples. The Hf-O bond in Hf/H20849mp/H208504 was more stable than the Hf-N bond in Hf/H20849NEt2/H208504, and the bulky OCMeEt2 ligand in Hf/H20849mp/H208504 was more effective in shielding the Hf atoms than the NEt2 ligand in Hf/H20849NEt2/H208504.
